read.cue: your teammates already have the puck pressured and the slot covered, leaving the net-front man alone

interaction.prompt: The puck's in your corner. Read the ice and drag YOURSELF (the defence) to where you're needed most.

feedback.right: Yes. The slot is already covered, so the open, most-dangerous man is the one on the doorstep. Take the net-front away before the cross-crease pass.
feedback.wrong: Doubling up on the slot leaves the most dangerous man — alone on the doorstep — wide open for a tap-in. Cover the uncovered threat, not the one a teammate already has.

tip: Cover the most dangerous UNCOVERED man. Don't double up where a teammate already is.
why: Defensive-zone coverage is reading who's already covered and who isn't. The open man at the net is the goal-scorer — take him, don't ball-watch the puck or crowd the slot.
